verdict.rationale: Blink's own docs say you can "manage and edit files from the command line" and support Vim/Emacs-style key mappings, so file editing in the terminal is claimed. The pack never names a bundled local terminal editor, and nothing shows syntax or lint checkers running in the app; the command list (cat, grep, ls…) has no editor or linter, and scripting is limited to python/lua. Missing for 10: a documented local terminal editor (e.g. vim/nano) shipped in the app, any syntax/lint checker support, and hands-on corroboration of in-app editing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can edit files with a terminal-based editor and run syntax/lint checkers inside the app

citations.quote: Manage and edit files from the command line, check on your network or download files.
Some like Caps as Esc on Vim, others Cmd as Ctrl on Emacs. _Blink champions them all_.
You can call commands individually, or use small scripts using python or lua.
